node-1.label: Irregularly linear, rusty-brown, atrophic, streaklike plaque extending from right shoulder to right biceps

node-2.label: The plaque ended in an arborizing purple plaque with scattered, slightly indurated, irregular papules within it; no warmth, thrills, or pulsations across the affected area.

node-3.label: Patient is a man in his 80s with an 18-month history of skin changes and mild tingling sensation within the lesion; he denied any triggers, causes, aggravating or alleviating factors, and had not attempted any treatments.

node-4.label: Review of systems was negative except easy bruising; current medications include finasteride, montelukast, enalapril, and metoprolol; medical history significant for right total reverse shoulder replacement 5 years prior.

node-5.label: Apart from the described lesion, physical examination was unremarkable, with full range of motion of the right shoulder.

why.why: The pathologist's analysis explicitly states that the biopsy findings are sufficient to diagnose intralymphatic histiocytosis and to exclude linear morphea/scleroderma, because the CD68+ histiocytic infiltrate within D2-40 highlighted lymphatic vessels lacks the sclerotic collagen pattern of morphea. The clinical features are also atypical for morphea. Confidence is reduced from 0.05 to 0.01.

The pathologist's confirmation of intralymphatic histiocytosis, a benign histiocytic disorder, makes malignant skin infiltration very unlikely. The dense CD68+ histiocytic infiltrate within lymphatic vessels is characteristic of a reactive histiocytic process rather than a malignant population. Confidence is reduced from 0.2 to 0.1.

Although D2-40 highlighted lymphatic vessels indicate lymphatic involvement, the pathologist's diagnosis of intralymphatic histiocytosis shifts the process to a histiocytic disorder within lymphatics rather than a primary low-flow vascular malformation. Confidence is reduced from 0.25 to 0.10.

The pathologist's analysis explicitly excludes post-surgical/trauma fibrosis because the biopsy shows a histiocytic infiltrate within lymphatic vessels rather than fibrotic scar tissue; the 5-year interval after shoulder replacement and full range of motion also argue against this. Confidence is reduced from 0.02 to 0.01.

node-12.label: Biopsy lacks sclerotic collagen pattern characteristic of morphea

why.why: The pathologist's analysis states that the biopsy findings—CD68+ histiocytes within D2-40 highlighted lymphatic vessels without sclerotic collagen—are sufficient to diagnose intralymphatic histiocytosis and to exclude linear morphea/scleroderma and post-surgical fibrosis. This directly confirms the hallmark histopathological feature, and the clinical features (arborizing purple plaque, easy bruising, ipsilateral shoulder replacement) further support it. Pending autoimmune serology and S100/CD1a/factor XIIIa immunohistochemistry leave a small residual uncertainty, so confidence is raised to 0.85.

attrs.why: The pathologist noted that S100/CD1a/factor XIIIa immunohistochemistry and autoimmune serology are still pending, so Langerhans cell histiocytosis cannot be completely excluded; however, the characteristic intralymphatic CD68+ histiocytic infiltrate is already diagnostic of intralymphatic histiocytosis and the clinical picture is not typical of Langerhans cell histiocytosis, so confidence remains low.
